metas.name: Buenos Aires - Small Lakes
metas.note: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Butia Yatay Palm - Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar
metas.note: The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Caranday Palm - Sierras de Córdoba
metas.note: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Caranday Wax Palm - Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.
metas.note: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Cardon - Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy.
metas.note: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Central Argentina - Flat, barren landscape
metas.note: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Chaco and Formosa - Sandy Soil
metas.note: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Corn - Córdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.
metas.note: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in Córdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Entre Rios - Tree Plantations
metas.note:
The majority of tree plantations in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.

NOTE: Uruguay and southern Brazil have them as well. Make sure to look at other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: La Pampa - Caldén and grid
metas.note:
Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

Extra meta: A lot of roads in La Pampa are in a grid (meaning exactly North, South, East, West) which can be a good meta for this province (It's rare for roads outside La Pampa to be in a grid)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Macaw Palm - Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.
metas.note: The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Misiones - Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Pampas Grass - Pampas Region
metas.note: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Salta, Jujuy, Tucuman - Wild Sunflowers
metas.note: Wild sunflowers (Tithonia tubaeformis) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: San Luis - Needle Grass
metas.note:
Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

Creator note:not all locations will have the reddish pavement but will still have the Argentine needle-grass which from experience is pretty reliable for getting San Luis
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Sugarcane - Tucumán
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: TDF - Beech Forests
metas.note: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: TDF and Southern Santa Cruz - Flat grass
metas.note: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Toothpick Cactus - Catamara, Cordoba and the border of Chaco, Salta, and Formosa
metas.note: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Western Argentina - Mountains
metas.note: Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
